standard_prerequisites.name: Openness of a flat locally finitely presented morphism, and the dense open case with retrocompactness

standard_prerequisites.use: The first makes the image of each piece open so that it must meet the given dense open, and the second turns the retrocompact dense open case into the locally finitely presented case.

core_obligations: Reduce to the pieces of bounded fibre dimension: let W be the open subscheme containing every generic point of every fibre, note it suffices to treat W, and since it decomposes by the fibre dimension it suffices to show that the pieces of dimension larger than the bound are empty (proof lines 3033-3041).

Use openness against the dense open: the morphism is open because it is flat and locally of finitely presented, so if a piece of too large dimension were nonempty its image would be a nonempty open set, which must meet the given dense open, contradicting the bound assumed over that open (proof lines 3041-3044).

Reduce case (2) to case (1): in the retrocompact case one may replace the base by its reduction, where the dense open becomes scheme theoretically dense, and then the morphism is locally of finitely presented by the corresponding statement, bringing us back to case (1) (proof lines 3046-3050).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the pieces of the bounded-dimension open subscheme (proof lines 3033-3041).
Openness plus density gives the contradiction (proof lines 3041-3044).
Case (2) reduces to case (1) via the reduction of the base (proof lines 3046-3050).
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the relative dimension of a flat locally finite type morphism from the dimension assumed over a dense open, under either local finite presentation or retrocompactness of the open (statement lines 3019-3031, tag 081N-adjacent). The proof reduces to the open subscheme of the source where the fibre dimension is bounded, notes that it decomposes into the pieces of fixed fibre dimension, and uses openness of the morphism together with density of the given open to show that no piece of too large dimension can be nonempty; the second case is reduced to the first by passing to the reduction of the base. The Openness-against-density argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
